intents.description: Greets the patient and introduces self or role.
Explains confidentiality and its limits.
Asks an open question that invites the patient to talk freely.
Asks what brought the patient in or what the main problem is.
Asks when the problem started, how long it has lasted or how it has changed.
Asks how the patient's mood or feelings have been.
Asks about sleep.
Asks about appetite, eating or weight.
Asks about energy or tiredness.
Asks about concentration, memory or focus.
Asks about loss of interest or enjoyment in usual activities.
Asks about thoughts of death, not wanting to live, self-harm or suicide.
Asks about a suicide plan, intent, preparations or past attempts.
Asks about access to means (tablets, pesticides, weapons and so on).
Asks what keeps the patient going, reasons for living, or supports.
Asks about thoughts of harming others.
Asks about hearing voices or seeing things others do not.
Asks about unusual beliefs, being watched, followed or controlled.
Asks about alcohol use.
Asks about drugs, tobacco or other substances.
Asks when the substance was last used.
Asks about past withdrawal symptoms, fits or delirium.
Asks about past mental health problems, treatment, or periods of elevated mood.
Asks about current or past medicines.
Asks about allergies.
Asks about physical illnesses or medical history.
Asks about illness, including mental illness, in the family.
Asks about work, living situation, relationships, finances or family set-up.
Asks about abuse or traumatic experiences.
Asks about pregnancy, periods or contraception.
Acknowledges or validates the patient's feelings.
Summarises what the patient has said.
Checks the patient understood, or checks own understanding.
Judging, blaming, dismissive, mocking or abusive language.
Cuts the patient off or talks over them.
